question: From which of the following countries did India borrow the parliamentary system of government?
solution:
The correct answer is** "Britain".** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• India has taken many features from various countries' constitutions like **Canada, South Africa, Japan, Australia, USA, etc.**
 
• **A parliamentary form of government **was chosen by India from Britain.
 
• In the parliamentary system, the government is formed by the political party that gets the most seats in the legislature or parliament during the federal election.
 
• **Features of the parliamentary form of government:**
 
 
• There is a close relationship between the legislature and the executive.
 
• Both executive and legislature are responsible to each other.
 
• The leader of this form of government is the prime minister, etc.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Indian constitution came into existence on** 26th November 1949.**
 
• Some borrowed features of the constitution from other countries:
 
 
• **Australia:**
 
 
• Concurrent list.
 
• Freedom of trade, commerce, and intercourse.
 
• Joint-sitting of the two Houses of Parliament.
 
 
 
• **Canada:**
 
 
• Federation with a strong center.
 
• Appointment of state governors by the center.
 
• Advisory jurisdiction of the supreme court.
 
 
 
• **Japan:** 
 
 
• Procedure establishment of law.
 
 
 
• **France:**
 
 
• Republic.
 
• Ideals of liberty, equality, and fraternity in the preamble.
